database_summary: Chinook-like music store schema (SQLite) with core entities: Artist, Album, Track, Genre, MediaType, Playlist and PlaylistTrack, plus business entities: Customer, Employee, Invoice, InvoiceLine. Row counts indicate a small transactional dataset (tracks ~3500, invoices 412, invoice lines 2240). Relationships are FK-based and typical: Artist->Album->Track, Track->(Genre,MediaType), Track<->Playlist via PlaylistTrack (many-to-many), Customer->Invoice->InvoiceLine->Track, Employee referenced by Customer.SupportRep and Employee.ReportsTo (org chart).

accepted.name: track_with_album_artist_genre_media
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Track.TrackId,
  Track.Name,
  Track.AlbumId,
  Album.Title AS Title,
  Album.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name,
  Track.MediaTypeId,
  MediaType.Name AS Name_1,
  Track.GenreId,
  Genre.Name AS Name_2,
  Track.Composer,
  Track.Milliseconds,
  Track.Bytes,
  Track.UnitPrice
FROM Track
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN Genre ON Track.GenreId = Genre.GenreId
LEFT JOIN MediaType ON Track.MediaTypeId = MediaType.MediaTypeId
accepted.description: Denormalized track-level relation enriched with album, artist, genre and media type metadata. Useful whenever queries need track attributes alongside album/artist names or genre/media labels (sales by track, playlist analysis, catalog listings). | Use for: List tracks with artist/album/genre labels; Filter tracks by genre or media type then aggregate sales; Join invoice lines to track metadata for sales analysis

accepted.name: invoice_line_with_invoice_customer_track
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId,
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceId,
  Invoice.InvoiceDate,
  Invoice.CustomerId,
  Invoice.BillingCountry,
  Invoice.Total AS InvoiceTotal,
  InvoiceLine.TrackId,
  InvoiceLine.UnitPrice,
  InvoiceLine.Quantity,
  (InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS LineAmount,
  Track.Name AS Name,
  Track.AlbumId,
  Track.GenreId,
  Track.MediaTypeId
FROM InvoiceLine
LEFT JOIN Invoice ON InvoiceLine.InvoiceId = Invoice.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN Track ON InvoiceLine.TrackId = Track.TrackId
accepted.description: Invoice line items enriched with invoice header, customer and track metadata. Useful for revenue, customer purchase history, track-level sales, and time-based invoice analyses. | Use for: Compute revenue by track/genre/customer/date; Customer purchase history and lifetime value; Invoice reconciliation (line amounts vs invoice totals)

accepted.name: customer_with_supportrep
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Customer.CustomerId,
  Customer.FirstName,
  Customer.LastName,
  Customer.Company,
  Customer.Email,
  Customer.SupportRepId,
  Employee.LastName AS LastName_1,
  Employee.FirstName AS FirstName_1,
  Employee.Title
FROM Customer
LEFT JOIN Employee ON Customer.SupportRepId = Employee.EmployeeId
accepted.description: Customer rows joined to their support representative (employee). Useful for support workload, rep performance, and customer contact listings grouped by rep. | Use for: List customers by support rep; Aggregate customers per support rep; Contact lists including rep info

accepted.name: artist_album_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Artist.ArtistId,
  Artist.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Album.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Track.TrackId) AS TrackCount
FROM Artist
LEFT JOIN Album ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN Track ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
GROUP BY Artist.ArtistId, Artist.Name
accepted.description: Counts of albums and tracks per artist. Useful for catalog size metrics, artist popularity baselines, and join-ready artist-level aggregates. | Use for: Catalog metrics per artist; Join artist-level aggregates to sales data; Identify artists with many/few tracks

accepted.name: monthly_invoice_totals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  STRFTIME('%Y', Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS InvoiceYear,
  STRFTIME('%m', Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS InvoiceMonth,
  COUNT(Invoice.InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount,
  SUM(Invoice.Total) AS TotalRevenue
FROM Invoice
GROUP BY STRFTIME('%Y', Invoice.InvoiceDate), STRFTIME('%m', Invoice.InvoiceDate)
accepted.description: Aggregated invoice totals and invoice counts by year and month. Useful for revenue time-series, period-over-period comparisons, and trend analysis. | Use for: Monthly revenue and invoice volume; Time series comparisons and seasonality

accepted.name: track_sales_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Track.TrackId,
  Track.Name,
  SUM(InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS TotalQuantitySold,
  SUM(InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.CustomerId) AS DistinctCustomerCount,
  MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS LastInvoiceDate
FROM InvoiceLine
LEFT JOIN Invoice ON InvoiceLine.InvoiceId = Invoice.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN Track ON InvoiceLine.TrackId = Track.TrackId
GROUP BY Track.TrackId, Track.Name
accepted.description: Pre-aggregated sales metrics per track: total quantity sold, total revenue, distinct customers, and last sale date. Useful for top-selling tracks, long-tail analysis, and inventory planning. | Use for: Top selling tracks by revenue or quantity; Customer reach per track; Recency of sales per track

accepted.name: playlist_track_with_metadata
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  PlaylistTrack.PlaylistId,
  Playlist.Name AS Name,
  PlaylistTrack.TrackId,
  Track.Name AS Name_1,
  Track.AlbumId,
  Album.Title AS Title,
  Album.ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name_2
FROM PlaylistTrack
LEFT JOIN Playlist ON PlaylistTrack.PlaylistId = Playlist.PlaylistId
LEFT JOIN Track ON PlaylistTrack.TrackId = Track.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
accepted.description: Playlist-track membership enriched with track, album and artist names. Useful for playlist content inspection, playlist-based analytics, and export of playlist contents. | Use for: Show playlist contents with artist and album labels; Analyze popularity of tracks within playlists

accepted.name: employee_org_hierarchy
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.EmployeeId,
  e.FirstName,
  e.LastName,
  e.ReportsTo,
  0 AS Level,
  e.EmployeeId AS RootEmployeeId
FROM Employee e
UNION ALL
SELECT
  m.EmployeeId,
  m.FirstName,
  m.LastName,
  m.ReportsTo,
  eh.Level + 1 AS Level,
  eh.RootEmployeeId
FROM Employee m
JOIN employee_org_hierarchy eh ON m.EmployeeId = eh.ReportsTo
accepted.description: Recursive hierarchy of employees mapping each employee to their chain of managers (manager levels). Useful for org chart traversal, reporting line queries, and aggregated metrics up the management chain. | Use for: Find all reports (direct and indirect) for a manager; Aggregate metrics up managerial chains

accepted.name: tracks_ranked_by_sales
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.TrackId,
  t.Name,
  COALESCE(SUM(il.Quantity),0) AS TotalQuantitySold,
  COALESCE(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity),0) AS TotalRevenue,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity),0) DESC) AS RevenueRank,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(il.Quantity),0) DESC) AS QuantityRank
FROM Track t
LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
GROUP BY t.TrackId, t.Name
accepted.description: Tracks ranked by revenue and quantity sold using window functions. Exposes rank values so callers can filter top-N downstream. Useful for top-K queries without embedding a literal top-K in the CTE. | Use for: Top-N tracks by revenue or quantity (downstream WHERE RevenueRank <= k); Compare rank by quantity vs revenue

accepted.name: customer_lifetime_value
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Customer.CustomerId,
  Customer.FirstName,
  Customer.LastName,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount,
  SUM(Invoice.Total) AS TotalRevenue,
  MIN(Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS FirstInvoiceDate,
  MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS LastInvoiceDate,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(Invoice.Total) / COUNT(DISTINCT Invoice.InvoiceId) END AS AvgInvoiceValue
FROM Customer
LEFT JOIN Invoice ON Customer.CustomerId = Invoice.CustomerId
GROUP BY Customer.CustomerId, Customer.FirstName, Customer.LastName
accepted.description: Customer-level revenue and purchase metrics: total revenue, total invoices, first and last invoice dates, average invoice value. Useful for CLV, segmentation, and retention analysis. | Use for: Customer lifetime value and recency/frequency/monetary (RFM) features; Identify high-value customers for marketing
